claim: Uveitis is characterized by infiltration of leukocytes into the uveal tissues.
source: Uveitis describes a heterogeneous group of inflammatory eye diseases characterized by infiltration of leukocytes into the uveal tissues.
evidence: This is a definitional statement about uveitis presented in the abstract.

claim: Uveitis associated with HLA-B27 is a common subtype of uveitis.
source: Uveitis associated with the HLA haplotype B27 (HLA-B27) is a common subtype of uveitis and a prototypical ocular immune-mediated disease.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: Local immune mechanisms driving human uveitis are poorly characterized mainly due to limited available biomaterial and technical limitations.
source: Local immune mechanisms driving human uveitis are poorly characterized mainly due to the limited available biomaterial and subsequent technical limitations.
evidence: This is stated as a gap in current knowledge in the abstract.

claim: This study provides the first high-resolution characterization of intraocular leukocytes in HLA-B27-positive and -negative anterior uveitis.
source: Here, we provide the first high-resolution characterization of intraocular leukocytes in HLA-B27-positive (n = 4) and -negative (n = 2) anterior uveitis and an infectious endophthalmitis control (n = 1) by combining single-cell RNA-sequencing with flow cytometry and protein analysis.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract, supported by the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Ocular cell infiltrates consisted primarily of lymphocytes in both subtypes of uveitis.
source: Ocular cell infiltrates consisted primarily of lymphocytes in both subtypes of uveitis and of myeloid cells in infectious endophthalmitis.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 1B and Figure 2.

claim: Ocular cell infiltrates in infectious endophthalmitis consisted primarily of myeloid cells.
source: Ocular cell infiltrates consisted primarily of lymphocytes in both subtypes of uveitis and of myeloid cells in infectious endophthalmitis.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 1B and Figure 2.

claim: HLA-B27-positive uveitis exclusively featured a plasmacytoid and classical dendritic cell infiltrate.
source: HLA-B27-positive uveitis exclusively featured a plasmacytoid and classical dendritic cell (cDC) infiltrate.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 2C and 2D.

claim: Classical dendritic cells were central in predicted local cell-cell communication in HLA-B27-positive uveitis.
source: Moreover, cDCs were central in predicted local cell-cell communication.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by CellPhoneDB analysis in Figure 4.

claim: Anterior uveitis primarily affects the iris and ciliary body.
source: Anterior uveitis (AU) primarily affects the iris and ciliary body and constitutes its most frequent type (approximately 80% of cases) resulting in permanent vision loss through, for example, secondary cataract, glaucoma, or macular edema (Rothova et al., 1996; Thorne et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Anterior uveitis constitutes approximately 80% of uveitis cases.
source: Anterior uveitis (AU) primarily affects the iris and ciliary body and constitutes its most frequent type (approximately 80% of cases) resulting in permanent vision loss through, for example, secondary cataract, glaucoma, or macular edema (Rothova et al., 1996; Thorne et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Anterior uveitis can result in permanent vision loss through secondary cataract, glaucoma, or macular edema.
source: Anterior uveitis (AU) primarily affects the iris and ciliary body and constitutes its most frequent type (approximately 80% of cases) resulting in permanent vision loss through, for example, secondary cataract, glaucoma, or macular edema (Rothova et al., 1996; Thorne et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Acute anterior uveitis associated with HLA-B27 is the most common and often severe form of uveitis.
source: Acute anterior uveitis (AAU) associated with the HLA haplotype B27 (B27+ AAU) is the most common and often severe form of uveitis.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Typical clinical features of acute anterior uveitis include acute onset of discomfort, eye redness, tearing, visual impairment, and excessive cellular infiltration in the aqueous humor.
source: Its typical clinical features include acute onset of discomfort, eye redness, tearing, visual impairment, and excessive cellular infiltration in the aqueous humor (AqH; ie, the intraocular liquid of the anterior chamber) that is devoid of immune cells under non-diseased conditions.
evidence: This is stated as established clinical knowledge in the introduction.

claim: The aqueous humor is devoid of immune cells under non-diseased conditions.
source: Its typical clinical features include acute onset of discomfort, eye redness, tearing, visual impairment, and excessive cellular infiltration in the aqueous humor (AqH; ie, the intraocular liquid of the anterior chamber) that is devoid of immune cells under non-diseased conditions.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: The prevalence of the HLA-B27 haplotype is approximately 8-10% among Caucasians.
source: The prevalence of the HLA-B27 haplotype is approximately 8–10% among Caucasians and 40–70% among AAU patients (Kopplin et al., 2016) and thus represents a strong genetic risk factor for AAU (Brewerton et al., 1973; Huhtinen and Karma, 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: The prevalence of the HLA-B27 haplotype is 40-70% among AAU patients.
source: The prevalence of the HLA-B27 haplotype is approximately 8–10% among Caucasians and 40–70% among AAU patients (Kopplin et al., 2016) and thus represents a strong genetic risk factor for AAU (Brewerton et al., 1973; Huhtinen and Karma, 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: HLA-B27 represents a strong genetic risk factor for acute anterior uveitis.
source: The prevalence of the HLA-B27 haplotype is approximately 8–10% among Caucasians and 40–70% among AAU patients (Kopplin et al., 2016) and thus represents a strong genetic risk factor for AAU (Brewerton et al., 1973; Huhtinen and Karma, 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The HLA-B27 allele conveys an increased genetic risk for spondyloarthropathies and inflammatory bowel disease.
source: The HLA-B27 allele also conveys an increased genetic risk for other immune-mediated diseases, including spondyloarthropathies (SpA) and inflammatory bowel disease (IBD).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: B27+ AAU is regarded as a prototypic ocular immune-mediated disease.
source: B27+ AAU is thus regarded as a prototypic ocular immune-mediated disease and, accordingly, its treatment is based on corticosteroids (Khan et al., 2015; Rosenbaum, 2015) and classical and biological disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs (Heiligenhaus et al., 2012; Bou et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with supporting citations.

claim: Treatment of B27+ AAU is based on corticosteroids and classical and biological disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs.
source: B27+ AAU is thus regarded as a prototypic ocular immune-mediated disease and, accordingly, its treatment is based on corticosteroids (Khan et al., 2015; Rosenbaum, 2015) and classical and biological disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs (Heiligenhaus et al., 2012; Bou et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: T-cell inhibition by cyclosporine A is beneficial in other uveitis entities.
source: Notably, although T-cell inhibition (eg, by cyclosporine A) is beneficial in other uveitis entities (Nussenblatt et al., 1991), it provides limited efficacy in B27+ AAU (Gómez-Gómez et al., 2017), suggesting a yet poorly defined role of innate immune cells in its pathogenesis.
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: T-cell inhibition by cyclosporine A provides limited efficacy in B27+ AAU.
source: Notably, although T-cell inhibition (eg, by cyclosporine A) is beneficial in other uveitis entities (Nussenblatt et al., 1991), it provides limited efficacy in B27+ AAU (Gómez-Gómez et al., 2017), suggesting a yet poorly defined role of innate immune cells in its pathogenesis.
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: The limited efficacy of T-cell inhibition in B27+ AAU suggests a poorly defined role of innate immune cells in its pathogenesis.
source: Notably, although T-cell inhibition (eg, by cyclosporine A) is beneficial in other uveitis entities (Nussenblatt et al., 1991), it provides limited efficacy in B27+ AAU (Gómez-Gómez et al., 2017), suggesting a yet poorly defined role of innate immune cells in its pathogenesis.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the cited literature.

claim: Immune cells infiltrating the anterior chamber of the eye can be observed clinically but are difficult to obtain for further analyses.
source: Immune cells infiltrating the anterior chamber of the eye can be observed clinically, but are difficult to obtain for further analyses.
evidence: This is stated as a practical limitation in the introduction.

claim: The invasive sampling of aqueous humor is rarely clinically justified.
source: In fact, the invasive sampling of AqH is rarely clinically justified.
evidence: This is stated as clinical practice knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Aqueous humor fine-needle aspirates are primarily applied for the verification of infectious uveitis.
source: AqH fine-needle aspirates are primarily applied for the verification of, for example, infectious uveitis (Chronopoulos et al., 2016) and rarely to unravel the pathogenesis of non-infectious uveitis (Greiner and Amer, 2008; Chen et al., 2015; de Groot-Mijnes et al., 2015; Zhao et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Aqueous humor fine-needle aspirates are rarely used to unravel the pathogenesis of non-infectious uveitis.
source: AqH fine-needle aspirates are primarily applied for the verification of, for example, infectious uveitis (Chronopoulos et al., 2016) and rarely to unravel the pathogenesis of non-infectious uveitis (Greiner and Amer, 2008; Chen et al., 2015; de Groot-Mijnes et al., 2015; Zhao et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: A role of bacterial triggers has been proposed in acute anterior uveitis.
source: In AAU, a role of bacterial triggers has been proposed (Huhtinen et al., 2002a; Huhtinen et al., 2002b).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Phenotyping of circulating monocytes in patients with immune-mediated uveitis emphasized differences during the disease course.
source: In fact, phenotyping of circulating monocytes in patients with immune-mediated uveitis emphasized differences during the disease course (Liu et al., 2015; Walscheid et al., 2016; Walscheid et al., 2018; Kasper et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The microbiome, intestinal barrier dysfunction, and immune response have been suggested to contribute to the pathogenesis of acute anterior uveitis.
source: The microbiome, intestinal barrier dysfunction, and immune response have also been suggested to contribute to the pathogenesis of AAU (Rosenbaum and Asquith, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Soluble mediators have been analyzed previously in the aqueous humor of uveitis patients.
source: Soluble mediators (Bauer et al., 2020; Abu El-Asrar et al., 2020; Bauer et al., 2018; Bonacini et al., 2020) and infiltrating leukocytes have been analyzed (Denniston et al., 2012) previously in the AqH of uveitis patients, but access to samples and technical challenges remain the main bottlenecks toward better understanding the pathomechanisms in uveitis.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Infiltrating leukocytes have been analyzed previously in the aqueous humor of uveitis patients.
source: Soluble mediators (Bauer et al., 2020; Abu El-Asrar et al., 2020; Bauer et al., 2018; Bonacini et al., 2020) and infiltrating leukocytes have been analyzed (Denniston et al., 2012) previously in the AqH of uveitis patients, but access to samples and technical challenges remain the main bottlenecks toward better understanding the pathomechanisms in uveitis.
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Access to samples and technical challenges remain the main bottlenecks toward better understanding the pathomechanisms in uveitis.
source: Soluble mediators (Bauer et al., 2020; Abu El-Asrar et al., 2020; Bauer et al., 2018; Bonacini et al., 2020) and infiltrating leukocytes have been analyzed (Denniston et al., 2012) previously in the AqH of uveitis patients, but access to samples and technical challenges remain the main bottlenecks toward better understanding the pathomechanisms in uveitis.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation in current research.

claim: Single-cell RNA-sequencing studies have provided unprecedented high-resolution insights into immune mechanisms in various tissues.
source: Single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) studies have provided unprecedented high-resolution insights into immune mechanisms in various tissues (Heming et al., 2021; Wolbert et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The study screened 4980 total patients with any intraocular inflammation.
source: We screened 4980 total patients with any intraocular inflammation seen at our uveitis center.
evidence: This is a methodological detail reported in the Results section.

claim: The study included 11 patients with current onset of uveitis flare or endophthalmitis.
source: We included 11 patients with current onset of uveitis flare (n = 8) or endophthalmitis (n = 3) into this study, being untreated with topical corticosteroids for this flare (Supplementary file 1a), corresponding to a recruitment rate of approximately 0.18%.
evidence: This is a methodological detail reported in the Results section.

claim: The recruitment rate was approximately 0.18%.
source: We included 11 patients with current onset of uveitis flare (n = 8) or endophthalmitis (n = 3) into this study, being untreated with topical corticosteroids for this flare (Supplementary file 1a), corresponding to a recruitment rate of approximately 0.18%.
evidence: This is calculated from the data reported in the Results section.

claim: Cytokine analysis was performed in 10 of the aqueous humor samples.
source: In 10 of the AqH samples, cytokine analysis was performed.
evidence: This is a methodological detail reported in the Results section.

claim: Cellular infiltrates were analyzed via scRNA-Seq in aqueous humor samples of four patients with active B27+ AAU, two patients with active B27-AU, and one patient with active bacterial endophthalmitis.
source: Cellular infiltrates were analyzed via scRNA-Seq in AqH samples of four patients with active B27+ AAU, two patients with active B27-AU, and one patient with active bacterial endophthalmitis (Streptococcus pneumoniae); five of those samples were analyzed in parallel via flow cytometry (Supplementary file 1a).
evidence: This is a methodological detail reported in the Results section.

claim: Five of the samples were analyzed in parallel via flow cytometry.
source: Cellular infiltrates were analyzed via scRNA-Seq in AqH samples of four patients with active B27+ AAU, two patients with active B27-AU, and one patient with active bacterial endophthalmitis (Streptococcus pneumoniae); five of those samples were analyzed in parallel via flow cytometry (Supplementary file 1a).
evidence: This is a methodological detail reported in the Results section.

claim: The endophthalmitis patients were significantly older than B27+ AAU patients.
source: The endophthalmitis patients were significantly older than B27+ AAU patients (analysis of variance (ANOVA), p = 0.0157; Supplementary file 1a).
evidence: This is a statistical finding reported in the Results section.

claim: All B27+ AAU patients had associated spondyloarthropathies.
source: All B27+ AAU patients had associated SpA, and two of them received adalimumab therapy.
evidence: This is a clinical characteristic reported in the Results section.

claim: Two of the B27+ AAU patients received adalimumab therapy.
source: All B27+ AAU patients had associated SpA, and two of them received adalimumab therapy.
evidence: This is a clinical characteristic reported in the Results section.

claim: The two uveitis groups did not differ significantly regarding age.
source: Both uveitis groups did not differ significantly regarding age (ANOVA, p = 0.566), Antinuclear antibodies (ANA) status, frequency of systemic anti-inflammatory treatment, topical medication, previous ocular surgery, or time since uveitis onset.
evidence: This is a statistical finding reported in the Results section.

claim: The study obtained transcriptional information of 13,550 total individual cells.
source: Thereby, we obtained transcriptional information of 13,550 total individual cells and 1936 average cells (± 1411 SD) per patient with 830 average genes (± 402 SD) detected per cell (Supplementary file 1b).
evidence: This is a methodological result reported in the Results section.

claim: The study obtained 1936 average cells per patient.
source: Thereby, we obtained transcriptional information of 13,550 total individual cells and 1936 average cells (± 1411 SD) per patient with 830 average genes (± 402 SD) detected per cell (Supplementary file 1b).
evidence: This is a methodological result reported in the Results section.

claim: The study detected 830 average genes per cell.
source: Thereby, we obtained transcriptional information of 13,550 total individual cells and 1936 average cells (± 1411 SD) per patient with 830 average genes (± 402 SD) detected per cell (Supplementary file 1b).
evidence: This is a methodological result reported in the Results section.

claim: The cell recovery rate is in accordance with the expected 50% recovery rate of the scRNA-seq technique employed.
source: This is in accordance with the expected cell recovery rate of 50% of the scRNA-seq technique we employed (Zheng et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature describing the technique.

claim: After quality control, 13 individual cell clusters were identified.
source: After quality control, we clustered the single-cell (sc) transcriptomes of all patients combined and identified 13 individual cell clusters (Figure 1A and B).
evidence: This is a primary finding reported in the Results section and shown in Figure 1.

claim: Only hematopoietic cell clusters were identified in aqueous humor aspirates.
source: As previously shown in AqH aspirates of human uveitis patients (Denniston et al., 2012), only hematopoietic cell clusters were identified.
evidence: This is a finding reported in the Results section and supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Clusters were broadly classified into cells of myeloid origin (40%) and lymphoid origin (60%).
source: Clusters were broadly classified into cells of myeloid (40%; cDCa, cDCb, pDC, mature DC (matDC), granulo, myeloid) and of lymphoid origin (60%; natural killer (NK), γδ T cells (gdTC), CD8, regulatory T (Treg), CD4, naive B cells (Bc), plasma).
evidence: This is a finding reported in the Results section based on the scRNA-seq data.

claim: The marker genes expressed by the cDC sub-clusters did not fully overlap with previously described cDC type 1/2 markers from cerebrospinal fluid.
source: The marker genes expressed by the cDC sub-clusters did not fully overlap with previously described cDC type 1/2 markers used to identify DC subsets from cerebrospinal fluid (DC1: CLEC9A, XCR1, BATF3; DC2: CD1C, FCER1A, CLEC10A) (Heming et al., 2021) or peripheral blood (DC1: CLEC9A, C1ORF54, HLA-DPA1, CADM1, CAMK2D; DC2: CD1C, FCER1A, CLEC10A, ADAM8) (Villani et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a finding reported in the Results section comparing the current data to previous literature.

claim: The marker genes expressed by the cDC sub-clusters did not fully overlap with previously described cDC type 1/2 markers from peripheral blood.
source: The marker genes expressed by the cDC sub-clusters did not fully overlap with previously described cDC type 1/2 markers used to identify DC subsets from cerebrospinal fluid (DC1: CLEC9A, XCR1, BATF3; DC2: CD1C, FCER1A, CLEC10A) (Heming et al., 2021) or peripheral blood (DC1: CLEC9A, C1ORF54, HLA-DPA1, CADM1, CAMK2D; DC2: CD1C, FCER1A, CLEC10A, ADAM8) (Villani et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a finding reported in the Results section comparing the current data to previous literature.

claim: The endophthalmitis control patient showed almost exclusively myeloid lineage clusters with predominating granulocytes.
source: First, we assessed the endophthalmitis control patient and found almost exclusively myeloid lineage clusters with predominating granulocytes in accordance with an acute anti-bacterial response (Figure 2B; Figure 2—figure supplement 1; Engstrom et al., 1991).
evidence: This is a finding reported in the Results section and shown in Figure 2, supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: The cellular infiltrates in B27-AU and B27+ AAU patients' aqueous humor were of more lymphoid origin.
source: In contrast, the cellular infiltrates in B27-AU and B27+ AAU patients' AqH were of more lymphoid origin, reflecting their autoimmune etiology (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: This is a finding reported in the Results section and shown in Figure 2.

claim: Inter-patient variability was high when comparing B27+ AAU vs B27-AU samples.
source: When systematically comparing B27+ AAU vs B27-AU samples, inter-patient variability was high (Figure 2A and B), but several populations still substantially differed between uveitis subtypes (Figure 2C, Supplementary file 1d).
evidence: This is a finding reported in the Results section and shown in Figure 2.

claim: The CD8 and naive B cell clusters were reduced in B27+ AAU patients compared to B27-AU.
source: While the CD8 and naive Bc clusters were reduced, the pDC and cDCa clusters were more abundant in B27+ AAU patients (Figure 2C and D), overall indicating an influx or expansion of DC in this uveitis entity.
evidence: This is a finding reported in the Results section and shown in Figure 2C and D.

claim: The pDC and cDCa clusters were more abundant in B27+ AAU patients compared to B27-AU.
source: While the CD8 and naive Bc clusters were reduced, the pDC and cDCa clusters were more abundant in B27+ AAU patients (Figure 2C and D), overall indicating an influx or expansion of DC in this uveitis entity.
evidence: This is a finding reported in the Results section and shown in Figure 2C and D.

claim: The abundance of pDC and cDCa in B27+ AAU indicates an influx or expansion of dendritic cells in this uveitis entity.
source: While the CD8 and naive Bc clusters were reduced, the pDC and cDCa clusters were more abundant in B27+ AAU patients (Figure 2C and D), overall indicating an influx or expansion of DC in this uveitis entity.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data presented in Figure 2C and D.

claim: The abundance of broad cell classes quantified by scRNA-seq and flow cytometry showed a positive correlation.
source: Also, the abundance of broad cell classes quantified by scRNA-seq and flow cytometry showed a positive correlation (Figure 2E, Figure 2—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is a finding reported in the Results section and shown in Figure 2E and Figure 2—figure supplement 2B.

claim: The higher frequency of granulocytes detected in flow cytometry than in scRNA-seq might be due to the higher fragility of these cells during processing for scRNA-seq.
source: The higher frequency of granulocytes detected in flow cytometry than in the scRNA-seq might be due to the higher fragility of these cells during processing for scRNA-seq (Zilionis et al., 2019).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Across all clusters, multiple MHC class I and class II related genes were expressed at lower levels in B27+ AAU samples compared to B27-AU.
source: Across all clusters, multiple major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class I and class II related genes (HLA-A, HLA-DPA1, HLA-DRA, HLA-DRB1, B2M) were expressed at lower levels in B27+ AAU samples (Figure 3B–F).
evidence: This is a finding reported in the Results section and shown in Figure 3B-F.

claim: In B27+ AAU, the help and BcLin meta-clusters downregulated CXCR4.
source: Furthermore, in B27+ AAU, the help and BcLin meta-clusters downregulated one cytokine receptor (CXCR4).
evidence: This is a finding reported in the Results section based on differential expression analysis.

claim: In B27+ AAU, the toxic meta-cluster downregulated signs of cytotoxicity (GZMK, GZMH, LTA).
source: The toxic meta-cluster downregulated signs of cytotoxicity (GZMK, GZMH, LTA).
evidence: This is a finding reported in the Results section based on differential expression analysis.

claim: In B27+ AAU, the BcLin meta-cluster featured an increase of macrophage-inhibitory factor (MIF).
source: The BcLin meta-cluster featured an increase of macrophage-inhibitory factor (MIF), known to inhibit NK cell activity (Apte et al., 1998).
evidence: This is a finding reported in the Results section based on differential expression analysis, with citation supporting the function of MIF.

claim: MIF is known to inhibit NK cell activity.
source: The BcLin meta-cluster featured an increase of macrophage-inhibitory factor (MIF), known to inhibit NK cell activity (Apte et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: In B27+ AAU, the myeloid meta-cluster reduced expression of several interferon-regulated genes (IFITM genes).
source: The myeloid meta-cluster reduced expression of several interferon (IFN)-regulated genes (IFITM genes; Figure 3B–F).
evidence: This is a finding reported in the Results section and shown in Figure 3B-F.

claim: Elevated CTNN1 expression in mergeDC pointed to an involvement of the WNT/catenin pathway as previously described for spondyloarthropathies.
source: Elevated CTNN1 expression in mergeDC (Figure 3B) pointed to an involvement of the WNT/catenin pathway as previously described for SpA (Xie et al., 2016).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data shown in Figure 3B, supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Increased expression of Lyz and CALR within the mergeDC cluster suggested an activation of myeloid cells and simultaneously local counter regulating mechanisms.
source: Increased expression of Lyz and its cognate antisense AC020656.1, and CALR (Liu et al., 2016) and its antisense AC092069.1, within the mergeDC cluster suggested an activation of myeloid cells and simultaneously local counter regulating mechanisms.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data, supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Elevated expression of B4GALT1 in mergeDC potentially reflected the migratory capacity of dendritic cells.
source: Elevated expression of B4GALT1 in mergeDC, in detail cDCa and cDCb (Supplementary file 1f), potentially reflected the migratory capacity of DC (Johnson and Shur, 1999).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data, supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: The mergeDC, help, and toxic meta-clusters all upregulated C1ORF56 in B27+ AAU.
source: Notably, the mergeDC, help, and toxic meta-clusters all upregulated C1ORF56, an oncogene previously found induced in activated lymphocytes in IBD (Uniken Venema et al., 2019) and splenic NK cells (Crinier et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a finding reported in the Results section, with citations supporting the previous identification of C1ORF56.

claim: C1ORF56 is an oncogene previously found induced in activated lymphocytes in inflammatory bowel disease.
source: Notably, the mergeDC, help, and toxic meta-clusters all upregulated C1ORF56, an oncogene previously found induced in activated lymphocytes in IBD (Uniken Venema et al., 2019) and splenic NK cells (Crinier et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: C1ORF56 was previously found induced in splenic NK cells.
source: Notably, the mergeDC, help, and toxic meta-clusters all upregulated C1ORF56, an oncogene previously found induced in activated lymphocytes in IBD (Uniken Venema et al., 2019) and splenic NK cells (Crinier et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Elevated expression of PFDN5 was found in myeloid, toxic, and help clusters.
source: We also found elevated expression of prefoldin 5 (PFDN5) in myeloid, toxic, and help clusters (Supplementary file 1e), which was recently described as a specific marker for B27+ AAU associated with SpA (Kwon et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a finding reported in the Results section, with citation supporting the previous identification of PFDN5 as a marker.

claim: PFDN5 was recently described as a specific marker for B27+ AAU associated with spondyloarthropathies.
source: We also found elevated expression of prefoldin 5 (PFDN5) in myeloid, toxic, and help clusters (Supplementary file 1e), which was recently described as a specific marker for B27+ AAU associated with SpA (Kwon et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Elevated expression of CDC42 was detected in mergeDC, myeloid, and help clusters in B27+ AAU.
source: Furthermore, as previously shown in joint biopsies of SpA patients (Carlberg et al., 2019; Lam et al., 2019) and in association with autoinflammatory diseases (Carlberg et al., 2019; Lam et al., 2019), elevated expression of CDC42 was detected in mergeDC, myeloid, and help clusters and of CDC42SE1 in mergeDC, myeloid, help, and toxic clusters (Figure 3B–E).
evidence: This is a finding reported in the Results section and shown in Figure 3B-E, with citations to previous literature.

claim: Elevated expression of CDC42SE1 was detected in mergeDC, myeloid, help, and toxic clusters in B27+ AAU.
source: Furthermore, as previously shown in joint biopsies of SpA patients (Carlberg et al., 2019; Lam et al., 2019) and in association with autoinflammatory diseases (Carlberg et al., 2019; Lam et al., 2019), elevated expression of CDC42 was detected in mergeDC, myeloid, and help clusters and of CDC42SE1 in mergeDC, myeloid, help, and toxic clusters (Figure 3B–E).
evidence: This is a finding reported in the Results section and shown in Figure 3B-E, with citations to previous literature.

claim: CDC42 was previously shown in joint biopsies of spondyloarthropathies patients.
source: Furthermore, as previously shown in joint biopsies of SpA patients (Carlberg et al., 2019; Lam et al., 2019) and in association with autoinflammatory diseases (Carlberg et al., 2019; Lam et al., 2019), elevated expression of CDC42 was detected in mergeDC, myeloid, and help clusters and of CDC42SE1 in mergeDC, myeloid, help, and toxic clusters (Figure 3B–E).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: CDC42 was shown in association with autoinflammatory diseases.
source: Furthermore, as previously shown in joint biopsies of SpA patients (Carlberg et al., 2019; Lam et al., 2019) and in association with autoinflammatory diseases (Carlberg et al., 2019; Lam et al., 2019), elevated expression of CDC42 was detected in mergeDC, myeloid, and help clusters and of CDC42SE1 in mergeDC, myeloid, help, and toxic clusters (Figure 3B–E).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Many spondyloarthropathies-related risk genes were highly expressed in the BcLin cluster in B27+ AAU.
source: Many SpA-related risk genes were highly expressed in the BcLin cluster (eg, CLEC16A, IFNLR1), and in the mergeDC cluster (eg, IFNGR2, AHR) in B27+ AAU (Figure 3G, Supplementary file 1g).
evidence: This is a finding reported in the Results section and shown in Figure 3G.

claim: Many spondyloarthropathies-related risk genes were highly expressed in the mergeDC cluster in B27+ AAU.
source: Many SpA-related risk genes were highly expressed in the BcLin cluster (eg, CLEC16A, IFNLR1), and in the mergeDC cluster (eg, IFNGR2, AHR) in B27+ AAU (Figure 3G, Supplementary file 1g).
evidence: This is a finding reported in the Results section and shown in Figure 3G.

claim: Expression of genes involved in the detection of pathogens showed lower expression in the mergeDC cluster in B27+ AAU compared to B27-AU.
source: Compared to B27-AU, expression of genes involved in the detection of pathogens (eg, CARD9, TLR4) showed lower expression in the mergeDC cluster in B27+ AAU.
evidence: This is a finding reported in the Results section based on differential expression analysis.

claim: Most anterior uveitis-related risk genes were preferentially expressed in the B27+ AAU mergeDC cluster.
source: Notably, most AU-related risk genes were preferentially expressed in the B27+ AAU mergeDC cluster (eg, EYS, HLA-DRB5, ERAP1, and IL18R1).
evidence: This is a finding reported in the Results section based on GWAS risk gene analysis.

claim: The preferential expression of anterior uveitis-related risk genes in the mergeDC cluster indicates the relevance of dendritic cells in B27+ AAU.
source: Notably, most AU-related risk genes were preferentially expressed in the B27+ AAU mergeDC cluster (eg, EYS, HLA-DRB5, ERAP1, and IL18R1). This indicates the relevance of DC in B27+ AAU.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data presented in the Results section.

claim: The pDC and plasma clusters had to be excluded from cell-cell interaction analysis because of their small size in B27-AU.
source: The pDC and plasma clusters had to be excluded because of their small size in B27-AU.
evidence: This is a methodological detail reported in the Results section.

claim: The granulo and myeloid clusters had the highest number of predicted interactions.
source: In the resulting analysis, the granulo and myeloid clusters had the highest number of predicted interactions (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding reported in the Results section and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: In both uveitis groups, most interactions were between myeloid, granulo, gdTC, and multiple DC clusters.
source: In both uveitis groups, most interactions were between myeloid, granulo, gdTC, and multiple DC clusters.
evidence: This is a finding reported in the Results section based on CellPhoneDB analysis.

claim: Myeloid lineage clusters express the highest capacity for cell-cell interaction.
source: Myeloid lineage clusters thus express the highest capacity for cell-cell interaction.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the CellPhoneDB analysis results.

claim: B27-AU displayed many interactions between T/NK clusters with myeloid, matDC, and cDCb clusters.
source: B27-AU displayed many interactions between T/NK clusters with myeloid, matDC, and cDCb clusters (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a finding reported in the Results section and shown in Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The cDCa cluster showed widespread interactions in B27+ AAU.
source: In contrast, the cDCa cluster showed widespread interactions in B27+ AAU (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.).
evidence: This is a finding reported in the Results section and shown in Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The cDCa cluster might be involved in intraocular inflammation in B27+ AAU.
source: This suggests that preferential interactions differ between uveitis entities and that the cDCa cluster might be involved in intraocular inflammation in B27+ AAU.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the cell-cell interaction analysis.

claim: MHC class II-related transcripts were predicted to interact with surface molecules such as MIF or KLRC1 with immunomodulatory capacity.
source: Notably, when focusing on individual interactions of the cDCa cluster (Figure 4B), MHC class II-related transcripts (eg, CD74, HLA-E) were predicted to interact with surface molecules such as MIF or KLRC1 with immunomodulatory capacity and known association to autoimmunity (Figueiredo et al., 2018; Borrego et al., 1998).
evidence: This is a finding from the cell-cell interaction analysis shown in Figure 4B, with citations supporting the immunomodulatory capacity.

claim: MIF and KLRC1 have known association to autoimmunity.
source: Notably, when focusing on individual interactions of the cDCa cluster (Figure 4B), MHC class II-related transcripts (eg, CD74, HLA-E) were predicted to interact with surface molecules such as MIF or KLRC1 with immunomodulatory capacity and known association to autoimmunity (Figueiredo et al., 2018; Borrego et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The predicted interaction of cDCa with pDC clusters in B27+ AAU included the LAIR-LILRB4 and AXL-GAS6 interaction pairs.
source: The predicted interaction of cDCa with pDC clusters in B27+ AAU samples also included the LAIR-LILRB4 and AXL-GAS6 interaction pairs (Figure 4B) that exert immunosuppressive phagocytosing functions (Scutera et al., 2009; Brown et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a finding from the cell-cell interaction analysis shown in Figure 4B, with citations supporting the function.

claim: LAIR-LILRB4 and AXL-GAS6 interaction pairs exert immunosuppressive phagocytosing functions.
source: The predicted interaction of cDCa with pDC clusters in B27+ AAU samples also included the LAIR-LILRB4 and AXL-GAS6 interaction pairs (Figure 4B) that exert immunosuppressive phagocytosing functions (Scutera et al., 2009; Brown et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The most notable feature of all aqueous humor samples was a pronounced presence of IL-6 and IL-1 receptor antagonist.
source: Several cytokines were below detection limits, and the most notable feature of all these samples was a pronounced presence of interleukin (IL)-6 and IL-1 receptor antagonist (IL-1RA).
evidence: This is a finding from the cytokine analysis reported in the Results section.

claim: High levels of immunosuppressive IL1-RA in aqueous humor of uveitis/endophthalmitis patients have been shown in B27+ AAU patients.
source: High levels of immunosuppressive IL1-RA in AqH of uveitis/endophthalmitis patients have also been shown in B27+ AAU patients (Zhao et al., 2015; de Vos et al., 1994; Planck et al., 2012) and may reflect the immune-privileged microenvironment in the anterior chamber (Zhao et al., 2015; de Vos et al., 1994; Planck et al., 2012; Dana et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: High levels of IL1-RA may reflect the immune-privileged microenvironment in the anterior chamber.
source: High levels of immunosuppressive IL1-RA in AqH of uveitis/endophthalmitis patients have also been shown in B27+ AAU patients (Zhao et al., 2015; de Vos et al., 1994; Planck et al., 2012) and may reflect the immune-privileged microenvironment in the anterior chamber (Zhao et al., 2015; de Vos et al., 1994; Planck et al., 2012; Dana et al., 1998).
evidence: This is an interpretation supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The cytokine milieu in endophthalmitis was characterized by innate-related IL-6, TNF-α, and IL-1β.
source: The cytokine milieu in endophthalmitis was characterized by innate-related IL-6, tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α, and IL-1β (Supplementary file 1h), which are involved in ocular barrier breakdown and leukocyte recruitment into ocular tissue (Hao et al., 2016; Feys et al., 1994; Giese et al., 1998).
evidence: This is a finding from the cytokine analysis, with citations supporting the function of these cytokines.

claim: IL-6, TNF-α, and IL-1β are involved in ocular barrier breakdown and leukocyte recruitment into ocular tissue.
source: The cytokine milieu in endophthalmitis was characterized by innate-related IL-6, tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α, and IL-1β (Supplementary file 1h), which are involved in ocular barrier breakdown and leukocyte recruitment into ocular tissue (Hao et al., 2016; Feys et al., 1994; Giese et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The interindividual heterogeneity of cytokine patterns was high across uveitis entities.
source: Across uveitis entities, the interindividual heterogeneity of cytokine patterns was high (Figure 4C and D).
evidence: This is a finding from the cytokine analysis shown in Figure 4C and D.

claim: The B27+ AAU group showed significantly increased levels of IL-2, IL-6, IL-18, IL-22, IL-1β, and IFN-γ compared to B27-AU.
source: When comparing uveitis entities, the B27+ AAU group showed significantly increased levels of IL-2, IL-6, IL-18, IL-22, IL-1β, and interferon (IFN)-γ (Figure 4C and D).
evidence: This is a finding from the cytokine analysis shown in Figure 4C and D.

claim: Single-cell transcriptomics is generally prone to false negatives.
source: Single-cell transcriptomics is generally prone to false negatives (Vieth et al., 2019), and stromal cells and resident immune cells in the iris can also express proinflammatory cytokines (Miyamoto et al., 1999), which may explain the discrepancy between techniques.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Stromal cells and resident immune cells in the iris can express proinflammatory cytokines.
source: Single-cell transcriptomics is generally prone to false negatives (Vieth et al., 2019), and stromal cells and resident immune cells in the iris can also express proinflammatory cytokines (Miyamoto et al., 1999), which may explain the discrepancy between techniques.
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Significantly elevated IL-1RA and IFN-γ levels were found in the serum of B27+ AAU compared to B27-AU patients.
source: There, we found significantly elevated IL-1RA and IFN-γ levels in the serum of B27+ AAU as compared to B27-AU patients (Figure 4—figure supplement 2B,C; Supplementary file 1i).
evidence: This is a finding from the serum cytokine analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2B,C.

claim: Elevated serum IFN-γ indicates a potential role of IFN-γ in both intraocular and systemic immune response during uveitis activity in patients with spondyloarthropathies.
source: This indicates a potential role of IFN-γ in both intraocular and systemic immune response during uveitis activity in patients with SpA.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the serum cytokine data.

claim: Intraocular leukocytes are transcriptionally and compositionally different from blood.
source: By making scRNA-seq per se applicable to the AqH, we found that intraocular leukocytes are transcriptionally and compositionally different not only from blood (Zheng et al., 2017) but also from other tissues affected by autoimmune diseases such as synovial fluid in rheumatoid arthritis (Stephenson et al., 2018) or cerebrospinal fluid in multiple sclerosis (Schafflick et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Discussion, supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Intraocular leukocytes are transcriptionally and compositionally different from synovial fluid in rheumatoid arthritis.
source: By making scRNA-seq per se applicable to the AqH, we found that intraocular leukocytes are transcriptionally and compositionally different not only from blood (Zheng et al., 2017) but also from other tissues affected by autoimmune diseases such as synovial fluid in rheumatoid arthritis (Stephenson et al., 2018) or cerebrospinal fluid in multiple sclerosis (Schafflick et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Discussion, supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Intraocular leukocytes are transcriptionally and compositionally different from cerebrospinal fluid in multiple sclerosis.
source: By making scRNA-seq per se applicable to the AqH, we found that intraocular leukocytes are transcriptionally and compositionally different not only from blood (Zheng et al., 2017) but also from other tissues affected by autoimmune diseases such as synovial fluid in rheumatoid arthritis (Stephenson et al., 2018) or cerebrospinal fluid in multiple sclerosis (Schafflick et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Discussion, supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: T cells were more activated in B27-AU than in B27+ AAU.
source: We found T cells more activated in B27-AU than in B27+ AAU in accordance with the poor response of B27+ AAU to T-cell inhibition (Gómez-Gómez et al., 2017).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data stated in the Discussion, supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: The cell-to-cell network analysis revealed an involvement of TNFSF13B (BAFF), connecting naive B cells and plasma cells to cDCa.
source: The cell-to-cell network analysis revealed an involvement of TNFSF13B (BAFF), connecting naive Bc and plasma cells to cDCa.
evidence: This is a finding from the cell-cell interaction analysis stated in the Discussion.

claim: Enhanced levels of BAFF and APRIL in aqueous humor of AAU patients during inactive uveitis point to a role of intraocular B cells in AAU.
source: A previous study has shown enhanced levels of the B-cell factors BAFF and APRIL in AqH of AAU patients during inactive uveitis, pointing to a role of intraocular B cells in AAU (Wildschütz et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Naive B cells expressing CLEC16A were preferentially enriched in B27+ AAU.
source: Notably, naive Bc expressing CLEC16A (Rijvers et al., 2020), and plasma cells, expressing several SpA risk genes, were preferentially enriched in B27+ AAU.
evidence: This is a finding stated in the Discussion, with citation supporting the expression of CLEC16A.

claim: Plasma cells expressing several spondyloarthropathies risk genes were preferentially enriched in B27+ AAU.
source: Notably, naive Bc expressing CLEC16A (Rijvers et al., 2020), and plasma cells, expressing several SpA risk genes, were preferentially enriched in B27+ AAU.
evidence: This is a finding stated in the Discussion.

claim: Plasma cells and the intraocular plasma cluster do not express MS4A1/CD20.
source: Also, plasma cells and the intraocular plasma cluster do not express MS4A1/CD20 and, accordingly, SpA patients (with or without AAU) mostly do not benefit from treatment with the anti-CD20 antibody rituximab (Wendling et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a finding stated in the Discussion, with citation supporting the clinical observation.

claim: Spondyloarthropathies patients (with or without AAU) mostly do not benefit from treatment with the anti-CD20 antibody rituximab.
source: Also, plasma cells and the intraocular plasma cluster do not express MS4A1/CD20 and, accordingly, SpA patients (with or without AAU) mostly do not benefit from treatment with the anti-CD20 antibody rituximab (Wendling et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

source: One study identified CD14+ monocytes/macrophages and a separate CD14−/low BDCA-1+ (CD1c) myeloid DC population in AqH of patients with AU (Denniston et al., 2012).

claim: Dendritic cells orchestrate the interplay between innate and adaptive immunity.

source: Traditionally, three DC subsets were defined as classical (or myeloid) DC type 1 (cDC1) or type 2 (cDC2), and pDC (Merad et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: The study identified four intraocular DC clusters in two different uveitis entities.
source: We identified four intraocular DC clusters in two different uveitis entities.
evidence: This is a finding stated in the Discussion.

evidence: This is a finding stated in the Discussion, supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The elevated expression of IFN-γ-related transcripts indicates an IFN-γ-driven immune response during active uveitis.
